reviewer: root after literal proposal and primary predecessor review
reason: An operation code is a substantive hypothesis, but no literal operation example or fixed dictionary is nominated. GDT881 finds no shared-stroke example in its selected interface; an operation code need not share physical ink and is not refuted. Correct raw predecessor wording: GDT879 stopped at measuring complete plant graphs; it did not test a reusable text-binding rule. GDT346 already tested held composition, so a held combination alone is not novel. Fixed arbitrary symbol-to-operation assignments are legitimate; per-example repairs are the concern. Raw submission status describes its pre-add draft; IDEA000111 was actually added and is retained.

design.mechanism: iconic construction code with compositional operation parts
design.unit: a complete written combination paired with a local graphic configuration and one held novel combination
design.contrast: operation-compositional code versus whole-name code or layout-conditioned glyph shapes
design.prediction: After learning a small operation vocabulary from at least two literal, independently owned text-picture examples, a held new written combination should predict a predeclared graph operation such as a branch, attachment, repeat, or closure; the whole-name and layout-shape rivals predict no compositional transfer.
design.countermodel: The written combination may be an opaque name, while similar drawing configurations arise from page layout, scribe convention, or independent illustration generation. Both can mimic training examples without iconic semantics.
design.falsifier: A held combination fails to predict its predeclared operation, or the same operation prediction works only after assigning arbitrary glyph-specific meanings or selecting the target configuration post hoc.
design.principal_risk: The f100v/f101r motivation supplies no label ownership, literal operation example, or demonstrated shape law. GDT879 found no reusable text-drawing binding, so this remains raw and cannot be selected until those missing inputs exist.
design.source_motivation: Root-native observation: admitted GDT812 source 1006249 has local labels near diverse plant forms on f100v, while f101r has many forms but no local labels. This motivates a search question only; it is not a new finding or binding.
design.distinct_scope: Unlike GDT879, this does not seek a complete plant graph or require immediate text-picture alignment; it asks whether a small operation grammar makes a held written recombination predictive. Unlike GDT360/GDT346, it has an explicit held compositional drawing-operation falsifier.
design.smallest_test: Before any selection, locate two already admitted examples with literal local ownership and an operation-readable graphic relation; freeze one unseen written combination and one operation class, then test transfer using existing records only.
design.reopen_condition: Reopen only when two source-bound operation examples and one held recombination are available without new image admission or inherited German labels.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness, novelty, or positive evidence claim

blockers.detail: Need a concrete finite global operation/operand rule, observable rival and independently selected source example. Do not reject a code merely because its fixed symbols are conventionally assigned.
No source-bound writing operation and held graphic combination yet connects the abstract rule to a depicted construction. Joint inference is allowed; meanings need not be known separately first.

all_of.detail: A literal source construction and independently observable graphic contrast that distinguish at least two complete fixed models.
Freeze the global key and held graphic prediction, preserving exposure and existing family gates; no automatic GDT879 graph or botanical-trait rescue.

not_sufficient: A touched contour, shared page theme, fixed symbol arbitrariness alone, or the physical-interface result in GDT881.

relations.detail: Only a new source-opportunity question; not a general code falsifier.
Complete-graph measurement stop, distinct from a tested text-binding failure.
Held composition already has a primary predecessor.
